title: Four Hundred Twenty Five Thousand Dollars and Three Summer Reservations

blocks.text: Marcus had his finger pointed at my father’s chest when I came through the living room doorway. My father was wearing his old house slippers, but Marcus was wearing his brown bathrobe.
“Get out of here,” Marcus told him. “You are making this harder than it needs to be.”
My mother sat at the far end of the couch with her hands folded in her lap. Dana was beside her, laughing at something Marcus had said.
I stood there holding a white bakery box.
The chocolate cake inside had cost $28.99. I had bought it that morning because my parents had been married for fifty-one years, and I thought we could have coffee and cake together.
“Then take a walk. I need to speak with my parents.”
He looked toward Dana, waiting for her to say something.
“Then this should be easy. I need ten minutes alone with my parents.”

I put the bakery box on the coffee table. My father’s slippers were beside the chair, and his reading glasses lay on the armrest. Those were ordinary belongings in an ordinary living room. The only unusual thing was that my father seemed to need permission to use them.
“Come on, Dana. Let’s give her her little meeting.”
“Go with him,” I told her. “I’ll speak with you afterward.”
She looked at me as though I had insulted her.
Marcus finally walked toward the front door. At the doorway, he stopped and turned.
“You have to understand, we’ve been doing everyone a favor.”
He pulled the front door shut behind him.
My mother stood up and carried a kitchen towel to the counter. She folded it once, then again, carefully matching the corners.
“Would you like some coffee?” she asked.

Andrew Collins is a contributor who enjoys writing about everyday topics, people, and ideas that spark curiosity. His approach is simple and conversational, aiming to make stories easy to read and relatable. Outside of writing, Andrew follows current trends, enjoys long walks, and likes turning small observations into meaningful stories.
